messages:
Devon: paging — Acme dedicated VPC canary is showing a spike in 5xxs after pushing artifact redwood-inference:1.3.3 to canary subset (acme-dedicated-1/canary). Affects ~12% of their traffic. Root cause unknown, rolling back canary now. @Ravi you up?

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: INC-ACME-2026-03-15-01 — Canary failure detected for customer 'Acme'. Pager notified: Devon, Ravi.

Ravi: I'm on. copying steps. Do we have a pinned digest for the previous stable (1.3.2)?

Devon: yes, stable digest = sha256:7f3b9c2a4d6e9b1e0f3a5b2c6d9e8f1a9b0c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6. Canary digest 1.3.3 = sha256:aa11bb22cc33dd44ee55ff66778899aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899aa.

Maria: pinging Acme SRE: Sam — we saw increased 500s hitting the /v1/generate route from 10:12 -> 10:18 UTC. Customers on dedicated pool may see intermittent failures or degraded responses. We'll coordinate rollback and share ETA.

Sam (Acme): Confirmed, our product team flagged errors for ~5% of sessions. Please prioritize — some users are in a live demo.

Devon: plan: 1) remove canary traffic routing (stop new canary traffic) 2) pin canary nodes back to 1.3.2 digest 3) monitor for 5xx drop for 10m 4) if still bad, full rollback across the pool and drain canary nodes for deeper debugging. Starting step 1 now.

deploy-bot: Command executed: `redwoodctl route update --customer acme --pool acme-dedicated-1 --canary-weight 0`

Ravi: Confirmed route update applied. Canary weight -> 0. Existing canary requests draining (TTL 30s).

Devon: now pinning the canary nodes back to stable digest on the control plane: `redwoodctl deploy set --customer acme --pool acme-dedicated-1 --nodes canary --image sha256:7f3b9c2a4d6e9b1e0f3a5b2c6d9e8f1a9b0c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6 --pin true`

deploy-bot: Rollout job started: job_id=job-38294. Affected nodes: canary-01, canary-02. ETA ~90s per node.

Ravi: watching logs. attaching recent canary logs for canary-01:```
[10:15:23] ERROR inference: request failed: ModelRuntimeError: KV cache OOM at step 12
[10:15:23] WARN proxy: upstream reset by peer
[10:15:24] INFO health: mem pressure 92%
```

Devon: interesting — mem pressure spikes. Can we check quantization differences between 1.3.2 and 1.3.3? 1.3.3 enabled a different kernel path for int8.

Ravi: confirmed — 1.3.3 switched to optimized int8 kernel (opt-kernel-v2) which increased transient memory due to larger prefetch buffers. That makes sense in dedicated tiny canary nodes. We'll revert to 1.3.2 which uses opt-kernel-v1.

Maria: Sam — we'll aim for customer-visible errors to be resolved within 15 minutes. We'll update you when 5xxs drop below baseline. Apologies for the disruption.

Sam (Acme): Understood. Please confirm when it's safe to resume canary traffic.

Devon: canary nodes now pinned back (deploy job finished). `job-38294` succeeded. Verifying health checks and metrics.

deploy-bot: job job-38294 status: SUCCESS. Nodes updated: canary-01, canary-02 -> image sha256:7f3b9c...c5d6.

Ravi: metrics: 5xx rate across acme-dedicated-1 dropped from 4.8% to 0.6% in the last 3 minutes. Latency normalized. Looks good so far.

Devon: great. Next steps: 1) keep canary weight at 0 until we validate for 30m 2) open a postmortem ticket for the kernel / quantization regression 3) do not promote 1.3.3 to prod for Acme until patch.

Maria: I created INC-ACME-2026-03-15-01-comms and sent the first update to Acme SRE with rollback confirmation. I'll schedule a 1:1 war room with Acme for postmortem.

Sam (Acme): Thanks all. Appreciate the quick rollback. Please include recommended mitigations — we may want to pin artifacts ourselves while you fix.

Ravi: Action items logged:
- SRE: create PM ticket to bisect kernel change (ravi/sre-team)
- Runtime: revert opt-kernel-v2 behavior behind feature flag for small-vmem nodes (devon/runtime)
- Deplops: add pre-flight mem-pressure check to canary jobs for dedicated pools (devon/deploy)
- Customer: offer a control-plane knob to pin image on customer side (maria/pm)

Devon: oncall handoff: I'm available for 15 more minutes, then I'll hand to Ravi. @Ravi please take incident owner after 10:45 UTC.

Ravi: taking handoff. I'll watch the next 30m validation window.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-ACME-2026-03-15-01 updated: status=mitigated, owner=Ravi, severity=high, customer_impact=partial.

Devon: leaving notes here for the postmortem: reproduction steps, kernel perf toggles, affected commit d4f3b2a, patch candidate to cap prefetch buffer allocation.

Maria: I'll follow up with Acme by EOD with a timeline for the patch and offer a temporary pin UI in the console (manual option).

Sam (Acme): Confirming customers reporting normal behavior now. Thanks team.

Ravi: closing the immediate incident loop. We'll reopen if 5xxs creep back up. Postmortem owner: Devon.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-ACME-2026-03-15-01 closed by Ravi at 10:42 UTC.
